title: A right adjoint from objectwise representability
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] in fixed universes, with functor categories formed in a containing universe, and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor. Suppose that for every $Y\in\mathcal D$ the presheaf $H_Y:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Set}$, defined by $H_Y(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F(X),Y)$ and $H_Y(a)(b)=b\circ F(a)$, is representable: there exist an object $G_Y\in\mathcal C$ and bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,G_Y)\cong H_Y(X)$ natural in $X$. Then $F$ has a right adjoint: there exist a functor $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ and bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F(X),Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,G(Y))$ natural in both $X$ and $Y$. No triangulation, exactness, coproduct or compact-generation hypothesis is required.
